questions.prompt: Which item is an indigenous Kenyan percussion instrument?
questions.explanation: A drum is played by striking, so it belongs to the percussion family.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify indigenous Kenyan percussion instruments by name and use.

questions.prompt: How is a shaker mainly played?
questions.explanation: A shaker makes sound when its contents move inside as it is shaken.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe simple methods of playing percussion instruments.

questions.prompt: Which material can be reused to make a simple rattle?
questions.explanation: A clean bottle with seeds can make sound and also supports reuse of materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Select locally available materials for making simple percussion instruments.

questions.prompt: Which tool is useful for drawing with charcoal?
questions.explanation: A charcoal stick is a drawing medium that can make dark and light tones.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise charcoal sticks as a drawing medium for still-life work.

questions.prompt: What does smudging do in a charcoal drawing?
options: Spreads charcoal to make soft tones
questions.correctAnswer: Spreads charcoal to make soft tones
questions.explanation: Smudging gently spreads charcoal to create smooth light and dark areas.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of smudging in charcoal drawing.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is usually struck to produce sound?
questions.explanation: A drum produces sound when its surface is struck by hands or sticks.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the playing action used for common percussion instruments.

questions.prompt: Which action shows care for the environment when collecting sticks for charcoal drawing?
options: Leave sharp tools on the path
questions.explanation: Using fallen sticks avoids damaging growing trees and keeps the activity safer.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose environmentally responsible materials for creative work.

questions.prompt: Which object would be suitable for a still-life drawing lesson?
questions.explanation: A still-life drawing uses objects that are still and can be observed closely.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify suitable still-life objects for observation drawing.

questions.prompt: Which option names a non-melodic percussion instrument?
questions.explanation: A shaker mainly gives rhythm rather than a clear tune, so it is non-melodic.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify simple percussion instruments as melodic or non-melodic.

questions.prompt: What should learners do before using cutting tools to make an instrument?
questions.explanation: Safety instructions help learners use tools carefully and avoid injuries.
questions.learningOutcome: Observe safety precautions while making creative arts items.

questions.prompt: Which part of a drum is commonly struck to make sound?
questions.explanation: The stretched surface of a drum vibrates when struck and produces sound.
questions.learningOutcome: Name simple parts of a percussion instrument and their function.

questions.prompt: Which word best describes darker and lighter areas in a drawing?
questions.explanation: Tone describes how light or dark an area appears in an artwork.
questions.learningOutcome: Use basic art vocabulary when discussing charcoal drawings.

questions.prompt: Which netball skill sends the ball to a teammate?
questions.explanation: Passing is used to move the ball from one player to another.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic netball skills used in a mini game.

questions.prompt: Which netball skill is used to receive the ball safely?
questions.explanation: Catching helps a player receive and control the ball from a teammate.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise catching as a basic netball skill.

questions.prompt: Which colour is a primary colour?
questions.explanation: Red is a primary colour; green, orange and purple are secondary colours.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify colours into primary and secondary groups.

questions.prompt: Which option shows good catching technique in netball?
options: Use both hands and watch the ball
Hold the ball with one finger
questions.correctAnswer: Use both hands and watch the ball
questions.explanation: Watching the ball and using both hands makes catching safer and more controlled.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe proper technique for catching a netball.

questions.prompt: In a chest pass, where is the ball pushed from?
questions.explanation: A chest pass begins at the chest and is pushed toward a teammate.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the starting position for a chest pass in netball.

questions.prompt: Which secondary colour can be made by mixing blue and yellow?
questions.explanation: Blue and yellow mix to make green, which is a secondary colour.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply colour mixing knowledge when painting a netball picture.

questions.prompt: Which material is safest for improvising a netball for practice?
questions.explanation: Soft bundled cloth can make a safer practice ball than hard or sharp objects.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose safe local materials for improvising a ball.

questions.prompt: Why should players keep space between each other during netball practice?
questions.explanation: Enough space helps players move, pass and catch without bumping into others.
questions.learningOutcome: Observe safety while performing netball skills.

questions.prompt: Which action completes a good netball shot?
questions.explanation: Following through helps direct the ball toward the goal after release.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the progression of a standing netball shot.

questions.prompt: Which pair contains only primary colours?
questions.explanation: Red and blue are primary colours used to make other colours.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify primary colours during painting activities.

questions.prompt: When painting a netball, which choice best shows colour value?
questions.explanation: Colour value is shown by lighter and darker tones in a painting.
questions.learningOutcome: Use colour value to improve a simple painting.

questions.prompt: Which French rhythm name represents one crotchet beat?
questions.explanation: In French rhythm names, a crotchet is commonly spoken as taa.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret crotchet rhythms using French rhythm names.

questions.prompt: Which French rhythm name represents a pair of quavers?
questions.explanation: A pair of quavers is often spoken as ta-te because two shorter sounds share the beat.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret a pair of quavers using French rhythm names.

questions.prompt: Which pattern has two crotchet beats?
questions.explanation: Each taa represents one crotchet beat, so taa taa has two crotchet beats.
questions.learningOutcome: Read simple rhythmic patterns using French rhythm names.

questions.prompt: Which quality makes a rhythmic pattern easy to perform?
questions.explanation: A clear steady beat helps performers follow and repeat a rhythm accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe qualities of a good rhythmic pattern.

questions.prompt: Which tool is suitable for writing rhythm names in free-hand lettering?
questions.explanation: A pencil can be used to write and shape letters neatly by hand.
questions.learningOutcome: Write rhythm names using clear free-hand lettering.

questions.prompt: Which pattern repeats the same rhythm twice?
questions.explanation: The rhythm before and after the bar line is the same, so it repeats.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise repetition in simple rhythmic compositions.

questions.prompt: Why should rhythm names be written clearly on a chart?
options: So performers can read them easily
questions.correctAnswer: So performers can read them easily
questions.explanation: Clear lettering helps learners read, clap and perform the rhythm correctly.
questions.learningOutcome: Present rhythmic patterns clearly for group performance.

questions.prompt: Which sound group best fits one beat with two quick sounds?
questions.explanation: Ta-te has two quick sounds that fit into one beat as a pair of quavers.
questions.learningOutcome: Match spoken rhythm names to beat values.

questions.prompt: Which activity best helps a group compose a rhythm?
options: Clap and arrange taa and ta-te patterns
Erase all beats from the board
questions.correctAnswer: Clap and arrange taa and ta-te patterns
questions.explanation: Clapping and arranging rhythm names helps learners hear and build the pattern.
questions.learningOutcome: Create simple rhythmic patterns using known note values.

questions.prompt: Which choice shows respect during a rhythm critique?
options: Say what worked well and suggest one improvement
questions.correctAnswer: Say what worked well and suggest one improvement
questions.explanation: Helpful feedback is polite, fair and useful for improving a performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Give respectful feedback on rhythmic compositions.

questions.prompt: Which rhythmic pattern is easiest for Grade 4 learners to clap first?
options: ta-te taa ta-te taa ta-te taa
questions.explanation: A short pattern with two steady crotchet beats is simple to begin with.
questions.learningOutcome: Select simple rhythmic patterns for beginner performance.

questions.prompt: Which set shows the solfa syllables used in the Grade 4 melody lesson?
questions.explanation: The simple melody work uses the solfa syllables d, r and m.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify solfa syllables d, r and m in simple melodies.

questions.prompt: What do hand signs help learners show in melody work?
questions.explanation: Hand signs show whether the pitch is low, higher or lower in a melody.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret hand signs for solfa syllables in simple melodies.

questions.prompt: Which melody uses only d, r and m?
questions.explanation: The pattern d r m r d uses only the three required solfa syllables.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise simple melodies built from d, r and m.

questions.prompt: Which quality helps make a melody easy to sing?
questions.explanation: A good simple melody has a clear shape that singers can follow.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe qualities of a good simple melody.

questions.prompt: Which melody starts and ends on d?
questions.explanation: The first and last solfa syllables are both d.
questions.learningOutcome: Create or identify short melodies that begin and end on d.

questions.prompt: Why should learners listen to each other during melody practice?
options: To stay together in pitch and timing
questions.correctAnswer: To stay together in pitch and timing
questions.explanation: Listening helps a group sing the same melody accurately and respectfully.
questions.learningOutcome: Work collaboratively when creating and performing simple melodies.

questions.prompt: Which solfa movement is stepwise?
options: d to m to d only
questions.explanation: Stepwise motion moves to the next neighbouring solfa syllable.
questions.learningOutcome: Use stepwise motion when composing simple melodies.

questions.prompt: A learner writes d r m m r d. Which statement is true?
options: The melody uses only d, r and m
The melody is a colour pattern
questions.correctAnswer: The melody uses only d, r and m
questions.explanation: All the symbols in the melody are d, r or m.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse short solfa patterns for correct note choice.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows pitch discrimination?
options: Tell whether m is higher than d
questions.correctAnswer: Tell whether m is higher than d
questions.explanation: Pitch discrimination means hearing or showing the difference between higher and lower sounds.
questions.learningOutcome: Discriminate pitch using solfa syllables and hand signs.

questions.prompt: Which choice is the best feedback for a classmate's melody?
options: Your melody starts on d clearly, but the ending can be steadier.
Your work is bad and useless.
I did not listen at all.
questions.correctAnswer: Your melody starts on d clearly, but the ending can be steadier.
questions.explanation: Good feedback is respectful and gives a useful point for improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Critique simple melodies using polite and helpful language.

questions.prompt: Which command usually comes before 'set' in a sprint start?

questions.learningOutcome: Explain the sequence used in sprint starts.

questions.prompt: Why is body alignment important when sprinting?
options: It helps the runner move efficiently and safely
It removes the need to warm up
questions.correctAnswer: It helps the runner move efficiently and safely
questions.explanation: Good alignment supports balance, speed and safety during sprinting.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why posture and alignment matter in sprinting.

questions.prompt: Which action is part of a good sprint finish?

questions.learningOutcome: Describe the finish phase of sprinting technique.

questions.prompt: Which colour separates the main bands on the Kenyan flag?

questions.prompt: Why is the Kenya National Anthem sung during a school athletics event?

questions.learningOutcome: Recognise the value of singing the Kenya National Anthem during events.

questions.prompt: Which technique helps a sprinter react well at the start?
options: Listen carefully for the start signal

questions.explanation: Careful listening helps the sprinter respond at the right time.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply listening and reaction skills in sprint starts.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes acceleration in a sprint?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the phase where the runner builds speed after the start.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain sprinting phases using appropriate vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Which action shows proper etiquette when singing the Kenya National Anthem?

questions.learningOutcome: Apply proper performance etiquette while singing the National Anthem.

questions.prompt: Which choice best prepares a painted Kenyan flag for an athletics event?
options: Attach it firmly to a safe handle
Leave wet paint on the floor
Use a sharp stick as a handle
questions.correctAnswer: Attach it firmly to a safe handle
questions.explanation: A firm and safe handle makes the flag easier and safer to display.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare a painted Kenyan flag safely for display.

questions.prompt: Which arm action is suitable during sprinting?
questions.explanation: Forward and backward arm action helps balance and rhythm while sprinting.
questions.learningOutcome: Perform sprinting technique with correct arm action.

questions.prompt: Which pair best shows the order in sprinting after the start signal?
questions.explanation: After the start signal, a runner takes off and then builds speed.
questions.learningOutcome: Sequence basic sprinting actions correctly.

questions.prompt: Why should runners warm up before sprint practice?
options: To prepare muscles and reduce injury risk
questions.correctAnswer: To prepare muscles and reduce injury risk
questions.explanation: Warm-up activities prepare the body for movement and improve safety.

questions.prompt: Which gymnastics skill supports the body with hands and feet facing upward?

questions.prompt: Which surface is safest for practising a side roll?

questions.prompt: What should a learner do before performing a gymnastics roll?
questions.explanation: Checking the space helps keep the performer and classmates safe.

questions.prompt: Which action shows teamwork in gymnastics practice?
options: Take turns and support a partner safely
questions.correctAnswer: Take turns and support a partner safely

questions.prompt: Which patriotic song may be sung during warm-ups in class?

questions.prompt: Which body part should be protected most carefully during a roll?

Roll across the room without stopping
Throw a ball into a ring

questions.prompt: Which instruction would help a learner improve a side roll?

Hold a sharp object while rolling

questions.prompt: Which response shows respect after watching a gymnastics performance?
